text:
Nico Hischier is the kind of captain whose best work rarely shows up in the box score. New Jersey takes 58.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him on the ice, and NHL.com spent a headline last week on his "elite two-way game" before the Montreal game and the Nick Suzuki matchup.

His own finishing is right on schedule: nine goals on 9.06 expected, eight power-play points and a shorthanded goal against Washington. The gap is in everything around him. The Devils have scored 7.3 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back.

It is also a familiar story. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating 0.25 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice in 2025-26 (96th percentile among forwards) against top-tier competition, while his actual wins trailed his expected wins, 0.7 to 2.3. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a signature: 20% of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward. Our numbers project 60 points and 28 goals.
headline: Hischier is doing his part; the goals around him aren't
